subject: ventures/photo-editing
auditor: agent session (Claude), re-audit after the 2026-11-07 round; see run record
professional: a working event/wedding photographer who also edits video (culls 2,000 frames after a shoot, grades with LUTs, cuts reels); first checks: is the cull's sharp-at-100% pick right and does it spare deliberate low-key/high-key frames, is the straighten/tilt reading right, is ingest verified and non-destructive

evidence.correctness: Ran the code and recomputed against numpy, not the author's tests. Synthetic 320x180 gray frames fed to shootflow.frame_analysis. (a) _laplacian_variance vs a numpy 4-neighbour Laplacian .var(): 41824.04268277685 vs 41824.04268277683, 42130.3125 vs 42130.3125, 43182.3679 vs 43182.3679 (three frames, agree to 1e-12 relative). (b) noise_sigma_from_frame on flat 128 + Gaussian noise of true sigma 2/5/10 (measured std 2.018/5.013/9.991): tool 1.977/4.942/9.884; independent numpy Immerkaer mean-abs formula sqrt(pi/2)*mean|k|/6: 2.031/5.035/9.975. Within 2% of both. (c) dhash_hex vs an independent numpy 9x8 box-average implementation (bit = left cell > right cell): random frame 25d5dc35362c13dd = 25d5dc35362c13dd, 4x4 block frame 0000000000000000 = 0000000000000000, descending ramp ffffffffffffffff = ffffffffffffffff. (My first attempt disagreed because I had the bit direction and cell edges wrong; fixed against the docstring, so the tool was right.) (d) mean luma and exposure formula: tool 127.479 = numpy 127.479; exposure 0.937676 reproduces from the documented formula. (e) Tilt (new Hough/structure-tensor code since the last round): soft sigmoid horizons rotated by true 0, +2, -3, +5 degrees read -0.006, 1.982, -3.002, 5.002 degrees, confidence about 0.92-0.94. That is a clear improvement on the 2026-11-07 audit, which saw a 6 degree true tilt read 6.08 and a hard edge read 0. (f) End to end: `python3 -m shootflow.cli cull` on 4 ffmpeg images (testsrc2 sharp, same blurred sigma 8, near-black, near-white): keeper 1 (sharpness 0.883), blurred flagged blurry (0.178), dark and white flagged rejects with exposure 0.067 and 0.0; .xmp sidecars written next to each. All synthetic; no real camera RAW was available, so correctness is capped at 3.
evidence.completeness: README features checked this round: cull with --write-xmp (works, 4 sidecars written), frame metrics incl. new tilt and noise (work), tilt calibration on real photos (tests exist, one needs working PIL, see verification). Not re-run this round (ran last round and the code is unchanged apart from frame_analysis/calibration): checksummed ingest, local pipeline, LUT grade, reels/carousels. Stated gaps stand: RAW development, no app, look and scene stages are stand-ins. No NotImplementedError. A CLI, not an app; 3 against its own README.
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 517 tests, 19 s, 1 failure + 1 error + 1 skip. Failure test_workspace_health.test_unreadable_render_input_is_reported_for_review: chmod(0) does nothing as root (same artefact as last round, still unfixed). Error test_real_photo_calibration.test_tilt_crop_removes_corners_and_keeps_aspect: ImportError of PIL._imaging in this sandbox (system Pillow broken), an environment problem, but the test has no importorskip guard. Seeded mutations in frame_analysis.py, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean): M1 exposure target 120 -> 100: NOT caught, suite result identical to baseline; M2 tilt penalty in story_score zeroed (crooked = 0.0): NOT caught; M3 _LAPLACIAN_NOISE_GAIN 20 -> 10: CAUGHT by test_grain_does_not_pass_for_sharpness. So 1 of 3 mutations is caught, the same two gaps found last round (M1, M2) are still open, which is why verification stays at 2 although the new tilt/noise code is tested well.
evidence.craft: Read frame_analysis.py (metrics_from_frames, noise, dhash, Laplacian, luma stats). Clean, documented formulas with the Immerkaer derivation in the docstring and named constants, a real improvement. Defects: pure-Python per-pixel loops (the Laplacian and noise passes each walk 57k pixels and sort the full response list for a median) with no vectorised path; magic weights (0.6/0.4, 0.85/0.15) uncalibrated; parallel dry-run adapter/scheduler stack beside the real ffmpeg path (23,408 lines total in src/shootflow); `ruff check src tests`: 69 errors (41 auto-fixable), one more than last round. Worktree clean after audit.
evidence.claims: Library docstrings now match the code (tilt, noise, thirds). But the public page ventures/photo-editing/site/index.html is unchanged since the last audit: line 40 says 'The renderers are dry-run placeholders: ShootFlow does not yet render video or grade images', line 51 repeats it ('No. The renderers are dry-run placeholders'), and lines 34 and 47 tell users to run `shootflow cull FOLDER --out REPORT`, while pyproject.toml does not package a console script and the working form is `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m shootflow.cli cull`. The cull itself ran fine here, so the cull claim is backed; the render claim is false (understates; the pipeline renders and grades, shown last round) and the copy-paste command fails. The page does keep its disclaimer and no-upload statement. No fix landed between rounds, so 2.
evidence.fitness: Job: cull a shoot folder and get a ranked, XMP-tagged selection. It runs in one command and the sidecars open in Lightroom/Bridge by documented semantics, nothing is uploaded. Better than last round because tilt is now measurable and calibrated on real photos. Still: no install (PYTHONPATH invocation), no UI, RAW only via embedded preview, reels silent, never validated against a human's picks on a real shoot (VENTURE.yaml stage prototype). 2.
evidence.domain: Compared against Photo Mechanic/Lightroom cull practice (focus at 100% on eyes, keep one per burst) and DIT practice. Strengths: sha256-verified ingest, XMP star semantics, dHash burst grouping, Immerkaer noise estimation and structure-tensor/Hough tilt are standard methods, now implemented soundly. Departures: analysis on a 320x180 downscale hides critical-focus misses; exposure is mean luma vs fixed grey 120 with clipping penalty, so deliberate low-key/high-key frames are marked bad (the near-black test frame got 'blurry' as a reason too, a misleading label for a flat frame); eyes-open off by default. A pro would use it as a first pass, not sign off the cull.

defects.what: Public product page still says the renderers are dry-run placeholders and that ShootFlow does not render video or grade images (false), and tells users to run a `shootflow` command that is not installed. Unchanged since the 2026-11-07 audit.
Mutating the exposure grey target (120 to 100) or removing the tilt term from story_score leaves the whole suite unchanged; only the noise-gain constant is pinned. Same gap as last round.

Sharpness, exposure and tilt are read from a 320x180 gray downscale, so critical-focus misses are invisible and mean-luma exposure penalises low-key/high-key frames; a flat dark frame is labelled 'blurry'.
Two tests fail in a root/minimal sandbox without a guard: chmod(0) test (root) and a Pillow-dependent calibration test (no importorskip).
ruff reports 69 errors; pure-Python per-pixel loops with a full sort for the noise median; duplicated dry-run engine.

verdict: A re-audit one day after the first. The numeric core is reproduced by independent numpy code (Laplacian, Immerkaer noise, dHash, luma, and the new tilt meter recovering injected 0/2/-3/5 degree tilts to 0.02 degrees), and the cull runs end to end. It still does not meet the bar: the public page's false 'does not render or grade' claim and non-existent command are unchanged (claims 2), and two of three seeded mutations in scoring logic pass the suite (verification 2). Correctness and completeness are 3 on synthetic media; everything else is 2 because nothing has been tried on a real shoot.
